title: AutoFeatureTour tour (*.tour.json)
description: What to show: scenes of narration and steps. Names its platform; holds no URLs, credentials, launch commands or app-wide settings (stand-alone tours without "platform" may, for quick experiments).

$schema.description: This file's schema, for editors: a relative path to schemas/<type>.schema.json, or its $id URL (https://autofeaturetour.local/schemas/v1/<type>.schema.json). `aft schema <type> --write <folder>` puts a copy beside a file kept outside the checkout. The loader ignores it.

name.description: Run folder name (default: the file name).

env.description: Default environment (--target overrides; default: the platform's default).

fixtures.description: Fixtures from the platform's fixtures/: data ({data.x}), setup/teardown and off-camera steps.

story.description: The user story the tour verifies.

id.description: Ticket id, e.g. RMS-6142 (used in the run folder name).

items.description: One scene: narration over the steps that show it.

slide.description: A still slide instead of steps: drawn without a browser or app (no url, steps or camera), narrated like any scene. A tour can be all slides (an explainer) or mix slides with recorded scenes. Content blocks (body, bullets, code, table, columns, stats, flow, callout, image) are drawn in the order they are written.

kicker.description: A small label above the heading ("Concern 1 · Context limits").

heading.description: The heading (default: the scene title). **bold**, *italic* and `code` work in every text field.

subtitle.description: A line under the heading (a title slide).

body.description: Paragraphs of text (blank lines separate them).

items.description: Text, or { "text", "tone" }. A leading ✓ (ok), △ or ⚠ (warn), ✗ (bad) or ℹ (info) sets the tone too.

code.description: A code or text excerpt, monospaced.

items.description: Text, or { "text", "tone" }. A leading ✓ (ok), △ or ⚠ (warn), ✗ (bad) or ℹ (info) sets the tone too.

anyOf.description: A row with a tone (colours its first cell).

items.description: Text, or { "text", "tone" }. A leading ✓ (ok), △ or ⚠ (warn), ✗ (bad) or ℹ (info) sets the tone too.

rows.description: Rows: a list of cells, or { "cells", "tone" }.

items.description: Text, or { "text", "tone" }. A leading ✓ (ok), △ or ⚠ (warn), ✗ (bad) or ℹ (info) sets the tone too.

stats.description: Big numbers with a label ("13K" / "tokens in a 20-page rule set").

items.description: Text, or { "text", "tone" }. A leading ✓ (ok), △ or ⚠ (warn), ✗ (bad) or ℹ (info) sets the tone too.

flow.description: Boxes left to right. Between boxes: an arrow, or a connector written as its own item: "+", "=", "→", "&", "or", "vs" (["Rules", "+", "Form", "→", "Decision"]).

callout.description: The takeaway, in a coloured box: text, or { "text", "tone" } (default info).

image.description: An image (png, jpg, gif, svg, webp), relative to the tour file: beside the other content when it is written last, else a block of its own.

imageSide.description: false: an image written last is a block below the rest, not beside it.

note.description: Small print in the footer (a source, a date). For a takeaway, use "callout".

reveal.description: Build the slide in: each bullet, row, card, stat, flow box or paragraph appears in turn. true: one per sentence of the narration; a list: when each appears, as fractions of the narration ([0, 0.3, 0.6]).

dim.description: With "reveal": earlier items fade as each new one appears, so the current point stands out.

use.description:
A shared slide: platforms/

/slides/.json, slides/.json beside the tour, or a path to a .json file ({ "title", "narration", "slide" } or a slide). The other keys of this slide, and the narration of the scene, override it.

title.description: Shown on title cards and in reports.

narration.description: What the narrator says; the scene lasts as long as it does. Required unless "camera": false.

camera.description: false: off camera. The scene runs for real (unpaced, no narration needed), its checks still count and it is in the report and storyboard, but it is not in the video.

url.description: Path opened off camera just before the scene starts.

unresolved.description: Story items the generator could not map to the app; recording refuses until resolved.

todo.description: Work left for a person; recording refuses until removed.

hold.description: Seconds the scene stays after its narration ends (default: --tail, 0.75).

action.description: Actions: finding and acting on an element (default 10000).

retries.description: Retries for actions that time out (default 1).

onError.description: "skip": an action that can't be done is skipped (checks still fail). Default fail.

hooks.description: Test data, off camera: setup before the browser starts, teardown after it closes (teardown runs whenever setup ran).

items.description: A setup/teardown hook, run off camera with BASE_URL, RUN_DIR and RUN_TAG set.

cwd.description: Working folder, relative to the file.

output.description: Use what it prints (or the HTTP response) as data: "json" (an object merged into data) or "text" (trimmed, as data.<as>). Setup hooks only.

pin.description: With "output": pin what it created as an artifact of this name ({artifact.<pin>.<field>}; fields: the JSON object, or { <as>: text }), shown as "created by setup".

role.description: With "pin": what kind of thing it is (account, case…); {artifact[<role>].<field>} is the latest of that role.

secret.description: With "pin": fields that are secrets (redacted everywhere).

node.description: Script path, relative to the file.

pronounce.description: Narration substitutions: written form → how to say it ("RMS": "R M S").

trace.description: false: no trace.zip (it holds network traffic and DOM).

allowMocks.description: Permit "mock" steps. Mocked responses are listed in the report; scenes a mock answered in get a "simulated data" caption. Refused for "style": "verification".

mocks.description: Mock sets from the platform's mocks/ folder, applied off camera before the first scene (needs allowMocks).

trimWaits.description: Long waits (page loads, busy indicators, waitFor, waitForResponse, dismissed known issues): cut them (default), speed them up, or keep them. The narration is never cut. --no-trim keeps them for one run.

trimWaitsOver.description: Only waits longer than this many seconds (default 1.5).

leadIn.description: Seconds of each trimmed wait that stay, so the cut is not jarring (default 0.3).

slides.description: How slide scenes look (a platform's apply to its tours; the tour's win).

pages.description: Stand-alone tours only: a folder of static pages (relative to the tour file) served on a free local port for the run. It is the tour's baseUrl, so goto paths are files in it ("index.html?s=2"). Copied into the run folder with the tour.

style.description: Generation hint (verification, demo, training, explainer); the engine ignores it, except that an explainer gets no review of criteria.

draft.description: Generated with gaps; recording refuses unless --allow-draft.

items.description: A known app or environment issue: what it looks like, what to do about it, how to report it. Tours never mention it; when the issue is absent nothing happens.

name.description: Unique name; reports say "known issue <name>". An environment rule with the same name refines the platform's.

comment.description: A note for people (why it happens, the ticket).

when.description: What the issue looks like: a locator (popup, panel, banner, toast), a failing request, or a console message / uncaught exception.

status.description: HTTP status: 503, "5xx", "4xx", or a list (default any failure).

anyOf.description: A console error or uncaught exception.

paths.description: Only on pages whose URL contains (or matches /regex/) one of these.

do.description: Steps that dismiss it (scoped to the matched element unless "scoped": false; its UI must be gone afterwards unless "noWaitAfter"), "tolerate" (leave it; it does not fail the step through errors / appErrors), or "hide" (CSS display:none: fakes the app's state, reported as such). Default tolerate.

as.description: warn (default: in the report, the run passes), fail (APP, exit 5: this known issue must not happen here), silent (report.json only).

times.description: At most this many firings per run; after that it is a normal error again.

noWaitAfter.description: After its steps, do not wait for the UI to go.

scoped.description: false: its steps search the whole page, not just inside the matched element.

off.description: In an environment or a story: turn the platform's rule of this name off there.

issue.description: In a story: this works around a real app issue, for now. A passing run is then "passed with known issues", never plain green; a run where it no longer fires says the issue may be fixed.

workarounds.description: Known issues for this story only, after the platform's and environment's rules (the same name refines one, "off": true turns it off for this story). Mark a real app issue worked around for now with "issue".

review.description: The review of this story's runs: decisions about findings, carried over to every later run (they change how a result is read, never how the run executes).

items.description: A decision about one finding of a run of this story (made in the review, or by hand).

decision.description: script: the script is wrong (fix the step); workaround: a real issue, worked around for now (with a story workaround); app-issue: a real app issue, the failure stands; accept: expected or good enough (weak evidence, a known issue that is fine here).

by.description: Who proposed it, when not the person ("ai": an accepted AI fix).

workaround.description: The story workaround this decision added (undoing the decision removes it).

knownIssue.description: This decision marked the step "knownIssue" (undoing it removes that).

stage.description: Staging ("do / redo until here", aft stage): how the live app is handed off.

role.description: The role to hand off as (a second window with the saved login of that role); default: the tour role. --as overrides.

note.description: Hand-off text shown on the stage card: what to try by hand from there.

baseUrl.description: Root URL of the app in this environment.
Root URL of the app in this environment.

data.description: Values for {data.<key>} in login steps, fixtures and tours (credentials: username, password…). Strings may use {env:NAME}. Environment data overrides the platform data; fixture data overrides both.

launch.description: Start the app if it isn't running: one service or a list.

anyOf.description: A service the run starts when nothing answers at healthUrl (already up: used as is, never stopped).

command.description: Shell command that starts it (run from the platform folder).

cwd.description: Working folder, relative to the platform folder.

env.description: Extra environment variables ({port} is the free port).

port.description: "auto" picks a free port per run ({port}).

healthUrl.description: URL that answers when it is up (default baseUrl; {baseUrl} and {port} allowed).

anyStatus.description: Any HTTP status counts as up (default: 2xx/3xx).

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for it (default 120).

stop.description: false: leave it running after the run (slow-starting services).

stableTimeout.description: Max wait for a stable page (default 15000).

strict.description: A page that never settles is an APP failure (default: a warning).

shared.description: Other people and runs use this environment (QA): data a run creates there must carry {run.tag} (or be marked "readOnly"); validate warns when a tour creates untagged data. A shared environment is never reset.

reset.description: Hooks that put the environment back to a known state (restore a database snapshot): run by `aft reset` and `--reset` before a batch of runs. Refused on a shared environment.

appErrors.description: What browser-side errors during a step do: "fail" (APP failure) or "warn" (listed in the report).

ignore.description: Regexes of known noisy requests/messages: kept in network.json/console.json, marked ignored, never a cause.

mask.description: Blurred in the page before anything is recorded (video, screenshots, trace).
